diagnostic_evidence.quote: the generalized B\'ezout's theorem asserts the existence of a lambda-matrix $\Phi_{i-2}\in\poly_{i-2}(\R^{b\times b})$, such that $\Phi_{i-1}(\lambda) = (\lambda I-\widehat{B}_{i})\Phi_{i-2}(\lambda)\quad \forall\,\lambda\in\R.$
For a family of (non-commuting) matrices $A_{1},\dotsc,A_{d}$, we denote $\prod_{i=1}^{d}A_{i} = A_{1}A_{2}\dotsb A_{d}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Each Bézout factorization Φ_{i-1}(λ) = (λI-B̂_i)Φ_{i-2}(λ) appends the new factor on the right, so the accumulated factorization of Φ_{d-1} is (λI-B̂_d)(λI-B̂_{d-1})···(λI-B̂_2)Φ_0, in decreasing index order. The stated formula instead uses the increasing-order product (per the paper's convention ∏_{i=2}^d(λI-B̂_i) = (λI-B̂_2)···(λI-B̂_d)), and the final identification Φ_0 = S_{1,d}^{-1} relies on the latent-vector identity (eq:solventS), which is derived for and only valid for the increasing-order product; for the decreasing-order product actually arising, Ω_1S_{1,d}Φ_0 = Ω_1 fails. The formula is therefore false. Counterexample (b=2, d=3): Λ_1=diag(0,1), Λ_2=diag(5,6), Λ_3=diag(3,4), Ω_1=Ω_3=I, Ω_2=[[1,1],[0,1]]. All hypotheses hold (disjoint spectra; S_{2,3}=B_2-B_3 and S_{1,3} nonsingular; Van nonsingular with det=±900, so the fundamental polynomial exists uniquely). The construction gives B̂_2=[[5,-1/2],[0,6]] and S_{1,3}=[[15,-2],[0,15]], and the formula's right-hand side Φ̂(λ)=(λI-B̂_2)(λI-B̂_3)S_{1,3}^{-1} evaluates to Φ̂(B_2)=[[0,-1/30],[0,0]]≠0, violating the defining property fp(B_2)=0. (The true fundamental polynomial factors as (λI-B_3)(λI-B̂_2)·[[1/15,1/150],[0,1/15]], whose constant term is not S_{1,3}^{-1}; for d=2 the stated formula happens to be correct, so the defect manifests for d≥3, b≥2.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace eq:deffp1/eq:deffp by the correct decreasing-order factorization fp[B_1,calB_{-1}](λ) = (λI-B̂_d)···(λI-B̂_2)Φ_0, where Φ_0 is the inverse of a new reversed recursion (rows ω_i^T(λ_iI-B̂_d)···(λ_iI-B̂_2), built by consuming the B̂_j in decreasing order), which does not reduce to the S_{i,d} recursion; it must then restate thm:Chain, reprove the genericity (prop:wellpose analogue) for the new recursion, redefine χ_coef via ∥R^{-1}∥, rederive the growth bounds, eq:Gd, and the G_d-to-gap link used in deriving conj:sb, and define G_d in thm:sb via def:fp.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit formula for fundamental matrix polynomials (lem:Chain, thm:Chain) is false for d≥3, b≥2. The growth estimates derived from it (the displays bounding ∥fp[B_1;calB_{-1}](λ)∥ and eq:Gd in thm:interpolation) are unproven; the interpretation of G_d via χ_monoχ_coef/gap and the bound G_d ≤ (χ_monoχ_coef/gap)^{d-1} in Section 3.2 are unproven; the derivation of conj:sb and the application bounds eq:cor:eig, eq:cor:lr from thm:sb are broken; and thm:sb defines G_d by reference to the false formula eq:deffp (under the reading G_d = max of the fundamental polynomials per def:fp, thm:sb's statement and proof are unaffected).
issues.title: lem:Chain's explicit formula for the fundamental matrix polynomial is false (order-of-factors error)
issues.why_classification: A central stated result—the explicit solvent-product formula advertised in the abstract as the paper's generalization of Lagrange interpolation—is false as stated, and the paper's own computational device (the S_{i,d} recursion with eq:solventS) cannot be salvaged; every repair requires a new construction absent from the source plus restatement and rederivation of the supporting framework (prop:wellpose, χ_coef, eq:Gd, the Section 3.2 link) on which the interpretation of the main theorem and the conjectured corollary rest.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is clear that $f$ is a polynomial of entries of $\Omega_{i}$. Since $\Lambda_{i}$ and $\Lambda_{j}$ have disjoint spectra for $i\neq j$, we know that $f(I_{b},\dotsc,I_{b})\neq 0$, yielding that $f$ is a nonzero polynomial.

issues.failure_explanation: The trick of prop:nonsingular is that the determinant is a polynomial in the free variables Ω_i, nonzero at Ω_i = I, hence vanishing only on a measure-zero set. In prop:wellpose the factors of det S_{i,k} are not polynomials in the Ω's: they involve the recursively defined matrices Ω̂_j = Ω_jS_{j,d} and the inverses S_{i,k-j}^{-1}, so they are rational functions whose well-definedness on a full-measure set is itself part of what must be proved. Establishing that each factor is a.e. nonzero requires a downward induction in the rational function field (each det S_{j,d} is a nonzero rational function because it is defined and nonzero at Ω = I), which the proof does not supply; the invocation of 'the same trick' is an invalid inference as written.

failure_location.quote: we can perform the same trick in \cref{prop:nonsingular} to show that each factor in $\det S_{i,k}$ is nonzero generically, and in turn, $S_{i,d}$ is nonsingular generically.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hand-waved step by a rational-function-field argument: by downward induction on i, each det S_{i,k} is a nonzero rational function of the entries of Ω_1,…,Ω_d (well defined and nonzero at Ω_1=…=Ω_d=I), so its zero set, and the set where the construction is ill-defined, has Lebesgue measure zero.
issues.overall_effect: The almost-sure well-definedness of the chain construction (and of the formula eq:deffp) invoked in thm:sb's proof rests on this unproven genericity; without it, thm:sb's route through thm:interpolation's hypotheses is incomplete, affecting conj:sb and the application bounds transitively.
issues.title: prop:wellpose's genericity argument applies a polynomial trick to recursively coupled rational functions
issues.why_classification: The statement of prop:wellpose is correct and the proof idea (non-vanishing at the identity point) extends routinely to rational functions via a standard induction; the repair is local, requires no new construction, and preserves all downstream claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that all eigenvalues in $\Lambda$ are contained in an interval $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$ and eigenvalues in $\Lambda_{\perp}$ are outside $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$.
Notably, $\Lambda$ may consist of either a cluster of interior eigenvalues or a subset of exterior eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: lem:boundMP bounds ∥Φ(B_j)∥ by the maximum of ∥Φ(λ)∥ over the interval [λ_j^{(1)}, λ_j^{(b)}]—the convex hull of block j's eigenvalues—not over the set where those eigenvalues lie. The theorem only assumes the eigenvalues of Λ_⊥ lie outside the cluster interval; a b×b diagonal block Λ_j of Λ_⊥ may have eigenvalues on both sides of [λ_min^cl, λ_max^cl] (for an interior cluster this is unavoidable whenever the number of eigenvalues below the cluster is not a multiple of b, a situation arising in the paper's own interior-eigenvalue experiments). For such a straddling block the hull contains the cluster interval, so the written inference is invalid and the subsequent application of thm:interpolation (whose growth bound holds only outside the cluster interval) fails; eq:mainsb is not established for these configurations.

failure_location.quote: Note that all eigenvalues of $B_{j}$ for $d+1\leq j\leq m$ are in $[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\setminus [\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$, \cref{lem:boundMP} yields that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen lem:boundMP to a maximum over the spectrum of B_0 instead of its convex hull—its own proof supports this, since each φ_j(λ_0^{(j)}) is bounded by the maximum of φ_j^2 over spec(B_0) and then by max_{λ∈spec} Σ_j φ_j^2(λ)—and cite the strengthened lemma in thm:sb's proof; the union of the blocks' spectra is contained in the exterior set, so the proof goes through unchanged and eq:mainsb holds as stated.
issues.overall_effect: The main structural bound eq:mainsb is unproven, as written, for matrices whose Λ_⊥ blocks straddle the cluster interval—precisely the interior-cluster configurations advertised in rmk:sb; conj:sb and the application bounds eq:cor:eig, eq:cor:lr inherit the gap.
issues.title: thm:sb misapplies lem:boundMP: the max over a straddling block's spectral hull is replaced by a max over the exterior set
issues.why_classification: The root is a single misapplied lemma whose given proof immediately yields the needed stronger version; the repair is a local edit leaving the theorem's statement, method, and all downstream claims intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the probabilistic result for $c_{\Omega}$ comes directly from taking union bounds on the tail bounds above.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing t = √(2log(2(m−d)/δ)), the union bound over the d blocks Ω_i (i≤d) and the m−d blocks Ω_j (j>d) with the stated Gaussian tail bounds yields, with failure probability O(δ), c_Ω² ≤ b(dn−bd²)²(2√b+t)⁴/δ⁴ (up to the split of the failure budget): the factor max_j∥Ω_j∥ and the norm part of max_j∥Ω_j∥∥Ω_j^{-1}∥ each contribute a second power of (2√b+t), and the two maxima over inverse norms contribute bd and b(m−d). The stated bound instead has (dn−bd²)³ (versus b(dn−bd²)²) and only the first power of the norm term; it is not the union-bound consequence, and in regimes with small d(m−d) it is strictly smaller than what the union bound gives, so it is not a weakened restatement either. The claimed inequality is thus unsupported by the argument given.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, with probability at least $1-4\delta$, it holds that $c_{\Omega}^{2}\leq \frac{(dn-bd^{2})^{3}}{\delta^{4}}\Bigl(2\sqrt{b}+\sqrt{2\log\bigl(2(m-d)/\delta\bigr)}\Bigr)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the stated inequality by the correct union-bound consequence, e.g. c_Ω² ≤ b(dn−bd²)²(2√b+√(2log(2(m−d)/δ)))⁴/δ⁴ with probability at least 1−4δ (with the failure budget split over the four events), and adjust the one-sentence proof accordingly; all qualitative conclusions (δ^{-4} dependence, polynomial control of c_Ω) survive, typically with a stronger n-dependence than claimed.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative high-probability control of c_Ω stated in thm:sb is unestablished; the w.h.p. absorption of c_Ω into c_{b,d,n} used in deriving conj:sb (and hence eq:cor:eig, eq:cor:lr) lacks its stated justification, though a correct comparable bound follows from the same tail estimates.
issues.title: The high-probability bound on c_Ω² in thm:sb does not follow from the cited tail bounds
issues.why_classification: The erroneous quantitative sub-claim of thm:sb must be replaced by a different, correctly derived inequality—a contained, local recomputation that preserves the theorem's structure and all qualitative messages, but changes the stated guarantee and is not a mere typo or weakening.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under mild spectral gap assumptions---specifically, the multiplicity of desired eigenvalues does not exceed $b$---we provide a structural bound for \cref{eq:defangle} when $\Omega$ is a Gaussian random matrix.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that when the number of desired eigenvalues is not a multiple of b (e.g., 10 eigenvectors with b=3), augmenting range(Q) to a multiple of b makes thm:sb applicable. But thm:sb also requires (via gap > 0) that the augmented eigenvalues be partitionable into b×b blocks with pairwise disjoint spectra, i.e., all copies of each eigenvalue must lie within a single block. This packing can be impossible: with b=3, a cluster of five eigenvalues each of multiplicity 2 (10 desired eigenvalues) and all remaining eigenvalues of even multiplicity, any augmentation to a multiple of 3 produces blocks of size 3 that cannot be filled by whole multiplicity-2 classes, so some eigenvalue appears in two blocks and gap = 0; no augmentation makes thm:sb applicable. Thus 'multiplicity ≤ b' (the introduction's gloss of the hypothesis) is necessary but not sufficient, and the augmentation claim is false in such configurations.

failure_location.quote: We can simply augment $\range(Q)$ with a few additional eigenvectors in $Q_{\perp}$ so that its dimension becomes a multiple of $b$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the remark (and the introduction's characterization) to state the actual hypothesis: the desired (augmented) eigenvalues must admit a partition into groups of b with pairwise disjoint spectra—which holds, e.g., when the eigenvalues involved are simple—rather than merely having multiplicity at most b.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's stated scope—that thm:sb covers any target count via simple augmentation, and that the hypothesis is essentially 'multiplicity ≤ b'—is overstated; configurations with multiplicity ≤ b but no valid block partition are outside the theorem's reach.
issues.title: Claim that thm:sb 'still applies' via simple augmentation ignores the block-packing constraint
issues.why_classification: A local qualification of an unlabelled prose scope claim; no theorem, proof, or formal result changes, and only degenerate multiplicity patterns are excluded from the informal coverage statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this simple situation, $\chim$ can be bounded using existing results from random matrix theory; see~\cite{Rudelson2010}, for example.

issues.failure_explanation: For d=2 the ratios defining χ_mono are ∥λI−B_i∥/∥λI−Λ_i∥ with B_i = Ω_i^{-1}Λ_iΩ_i and λ a cluster endpoint. Since λI−B_i = Ω_i^{-1}(λI−Λ_i)Ω_i, these ratios can be as large as the condition number of Ω_i, while ∥B_i∥∥B_i^{-1}∥ can be close to 1: e.g., Λ_2 = diag(1000,1000.1), Ω_2 = [[1,0],[1000,1]] gives B_2 = [[1000,0],[100,1000.1]] with ∥B_2∥∥B_2^{-1}∥ ≈ 1.1, while at λ = 1000.1 the ratio ∥λI−B_2∥/∥λI−Λ_2∥ ≈ 100/0.1 = 1000. Hence the displayed inequality is false (and, since Ω̂_1 is similar to but not equal to B_1, the displayed equality between the Ω̂- and B-quantities is also generally false). What the surrounding argument needs—and what is true—is χ_mono ≤ max_i ∥Ω_i∥∥Ω_i^{-1}∥.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed bound by χ_mono ≤ max_{i=1,2} ∥Ω_i∥∥Ω_i^{-1}∥ (equivalently via the Ω̂_i), which follows from λI−B̂_i = Ω̂_i^{-1}(λI−Λ_i)Ω̂_i; the subsequent statement that χ_mono is bounded by existing random-matrix results remains valid with this correction.
issues.overall_effect: The illustration's claim that the χ_mono part is controlled by the condition numbers ∥B_i∥∥B_i^{-1}∥, and hence easily bounded by the cited random-matrix results as applied there, is wrong as stated; the intended conclusion survives only with the corrected bound via ∥Ω_i∥∥Ω_i^{-1}∥.
issues.title: The d=2 bound χ_mono ≤ max_i ∥B_i∥∥B_i^{-1}∥ is false; the ratios are governed by the condition numbers of the Ω_i
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction (bound by the condition numbers of the Ω's rather than the B's) repairs the false displayed claim and preserves the surrounding argument and qualitative conclusion; no formal result depends on the erroneous form.
